text:
Lars Eller is 37, on his eighth NHL stop (counting two in Washington), and scoring like a man who doesn't plan on leaving. The Panthers signed the Dane after a season in Ottawa, and he has ten points in 21 games, against 15 in 68 games last season. He scored in Columbus on Nov. 10 and then had the late equalizer two nights later as Florida came back to beat Detroit 5-4.

Our numbers are a little suspicious of the scoring around him. Florida has scored about ten more goals than its chances with him on the ice, and that kind of gap tends to fade. His own finish is normal (12.5%), and his chance rate is up from last season, so the individual part looks honest.

The concern is the one Evolving-Hockey raised a year ago: his team created little offense with him on (bottom 2% of forwards), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says the same. He's a 2018 Stanley Cup winner playing 16 minutes a night for a team that has won two of the last three Cups. The role is real. The point pace probably isn't.
